2.text: Playing ball is more common among the Maritime Chukchee, who live

3.text: in settled villages, and whose life is more regular than in the scattered, ever-

5.text: The Chukchee employ both hand-balls and foot-balls, which differ chiefly

6.text: in size (Fig. 196, a-d). The word used for the ball (qeˊpel), however, signifies

7.text: “kick,” “kicked thing,” and therefore is connected more closely with the foot-

8.text: ball. The outward appearance of the balls resembles very much that of the

9.text: balls used by Alaskan Eskimo. There are no particular rules for ball-playing.

10.text: The participants, mainly young boys and girls, are divided into two parties. The

11.text: ball is thrown or kicked by one party, while the members of the other party

12.text: try to catch it. Often the girls take one side, and the boys the other. Still

13.text: more frequently they all run about, trying to catch the ball as it flies from

15.text: Sometimes a whole reindeer-skin is folded and fashioned into a large

16.text: clumsy-looking foot-ball, and almost the entire population of the village joins

17.text: in tossing and kicking it about.
